    Library

    Source owners and provenance

    This distributed copy provides writing guidance. The situated version is a small navigable index of what grounds the core accounts and where to check a claim: attributable user input, selected originals, and precise source notes under personal. Personal records, chats, memory notes, authored philosophy, and observed work can contribute in different ways.

    Preserve author, time, message identity, and coverage needed to assess attribution, distinguishing original expression from later interpretation. Keep raw records with their existing owners; detailed histories, excerpts, provenance, and private detail belong there or in topical notes. Link rather than duplicate them or the common philosophy. Public bibliography stays with the common essays. State unknown or inaccessible evidence explicitly instead of inventing support to make the accounts look complete.
